progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: C1 and C2: reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium, rates and amounts, a flask settling into a steady mixture. Year 11: exothermic and endothermic, entropy as spread of particles and energy, delta G = delta H - T delta S with negative delta G meaning spontaneous (recalled in scene 3b).
progression.startsWith: A log burning to ash, set against a tree building sugar and wood from carbon dioxide and water.
progression.stopsAfter: Explaining why combustion and photosynthesis are non-equilibrium systems using the signs of delta H and entropy change, reading the sign of delta G, and keeping favourability separate from speed.
progression.nextLesson: C3: what a flask already at equilibrium does when it is disturbed (concentration and temperature).

teaching.task: Explain why a fire runs all the way to ash while photosynthesis cannot run on its own, using enthalpy, entropy and delta G, and predict a new combustion case.
teaching.causalExplanation: Giving out heat (negative delta H) and spreading out (more entropy) each favour a change; delta G combines them. Burning glucose has both terms pushing the same way, so delta G is hugely negative and the reverse is too slight to measure, so it runs essentially to completion. Photosynthesis is the reverse, so every sign flips and delta G is hugely positive; a leaf manages only because it is an open system with continuous light. Delta G says where a change is heading, never how fast.
teaching.conversationalApproach: One question (fire versus tree), the C2 flask recalled in one line, a staged worked example with the numbers in groups, a calibration bar so students can judge new values, a speed warning with a sugar bowl, and an unseen hydrogen case with a sealed tube.
teaching.openingDecision: Why does a fire run all the way one way, while a tree can build the other way?
teaching.understandingCheck: Work out delta G for hydrogen burning (delta H -572 kJ, T delta S -98 kJ), judge whether it ends as a mixture or nearly all products, and explain why a sealed tube that has not reacted does not contradict that.
teaching.curriculumScope: Explain why combustion and photosynthesis are non-equilibrium systems in terms of enthalpy and entropy changes (Module 5). Delta G is recalled from Year 11 as a tool. K, Q, delta G = 0 at equilibrium, the delta G to K link, activation energy and catalysts are deferred.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, coded energy-level diagrams, particle spreading, rate bars and a staged worked-example board. Colour key for this video: heat terracotta, spreading indigo, delta G dark ink, positive values on a warm tag and negative on a cool tag.
design.transitionPlan: Fire bar and C2 bar pair cut to the term card; the energy-level diagram ghosts as the particles scatter; the worked-example board is reused with every sign flipped for photosynthesis; the board cuts to the leaf and back; the attempt board replaces the aids; the steady flask returns at the end; scene crossfades with settle.

scenes.holdPurpose: Brief look at the ash and the two icons

scenes.visualReference: Coded energy-level diagram with surroundings box, then a 20-particle crystal that scatters

scenes.visualReference: Large formula delta G = delta H - T delta S alone on the board with a tick tag
scenes.teachingReason: Recalls the Year 11 combination in one formula and defines spontaneous

scenes.onScreenChange: The formula writes on large; delta H underlined terracotta and T delta S underlined indigo on "T delta S" with a "T in kelvin" chip; a teal tick and "negative delta G: runs on its own" appear; "spontaneous" writes beside the tick on its cue

scenes.visualReference: Board with short task, equation with phases, grouped givens, level diagram, particle spreading stage and staged substitution
scenes.teachingReason: Works the glucose example one stage at a time: heat, then spreading, then delta G
scenes.narrationCue: minus two thousand eight hundred and three / plus seventy-eight / twelve / two thousand eight hundred and eighty-one
scenes.motionPurpose: Givens appear on their spoken numbers, the heat stage then the spreading stage replace each other, and the substitution writes line by line to a boxed result
scenes.onScreenChange: The task and phased equation write on; "delta H = -2803 kJ/mol" and "T delta S = +78 kJ/mol" appear on their numbers; stage 1 shows the long terracotta drop with heat arrows; stage 2 clears them and the crystal and six O2 break into 12 particles with the "7 particles to 12" chip; the substitution writes with a pen bracket and the -2881 result is boxed in dark ink on "eighty-one"; two arrows point down together on "push the same way"

scenes.visualReference: Glucose result kept large with a long arrow, a shrinking reverse arrow and a two-label calibration bar
scenes.teachingReason: Gives students a rough scale so a new delta G value can be judged
scenes.motionPurpose: A long arrow runs to "all products" while a small reverse arrow shrinks to a dot, then the two-label bar appears
scenes.onScreenChange: The terracotta and indigo arrow runs down to "all products"; the reverse arrow shrinks to a dot on "measured"; the bar with "close to zero: a real mixture" (C2 flask thumbnail) and "hundreds below zero: essentially all products" appears on "rough guide" and stays

scenes.visualReference: Fire bar tagged non-equilibrium then static, compass arrow, coded sugar bowl and calendar clock
scenes.teachingReason: Joins the lesson to C1 and separates where a change is heading from how fast it gets there
scenes.motionPurpose: The fire bar empties and its tag changes to static, a heading arrow appears, then a sugar bowl sits unchanged while a calendar flips
scenes.onScreenChange: The fire bar returns with "non-equilibrium"; on "gone" the bar empties and the tag changes to "static: both rates zero"; a compass arrow "where it ends up" appears on "heading"; the sugar bowl and calendar clock appear with "heading is not speed" and the bowl does not change

scenes.visualReference: Glucose board returned with the equation reversed, updated givens, level diagram climbing and particles gathering into a crystal
scenes.teachingReason: Shows every sign flipping, including the double negative, so photosynthesis cannot run on its own
scenes.motionPurpose: A flip arrow reverses the equation, the givens change sign, the energy arrow climbs, and the substitution writes with the double negative ringed

scenes.visualReference: Coded leaf in sunlight with CO2 and O2 arrows, dashed open-system boundary and a separate respiration pair
